title: Relations (1-to-1, 1-to-Many, Many-to-Many)
description: Model real-world relationships in Prisma schemas, understand foreign keys, @relation attributes, and implicit vs explicit join tables.
completionLearnings: Mastered 1-to-Many relations: foreign key scalar field (authorId Int) vs relation field (author User)
Understood 1-to-1 relations and why @unique on foreign key turns 1:N into 1:1
Distinguished implicit M:N vs explicit M:N join tables with custom relationship attributes

concepts.title: One-to-Many (1:N) Relations
concepts.shortDescription: The fundamental relational pattern: parent holds array, child holds foreign key.

theory.summary: In a 1:N relationship (e.g. User has many Posts), the child table (Post) holds the foreign key scalar field (authorId Int) and the virtual relation field (author User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])).

targetHero.explanation: Post holds authorId foreign key pointing to id on User. User holds the posts Post[] relation array.

explanation: Scalar Field vs Relation Field: authorId is the actual column in SQL. author is a TypeScript-level relation field used for joins and typed includes.
Optional 1:N: Setting authorId Int? allows child records to exist without being bound to a parent.
theory.keyTakeaway: In Prisma 1:N relations, the model that holds the foreign key must define @relation(fields: [...], references: [...]).

mcqs.question: Which model holds the foreign key column in a 1-to-Many relationship between Author and Book?
options: Prisma generates an external join table automatically
mcqs.explanation: The "Many" side (Book) holds the foreign key pointing back to the "One" side (Author).

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Connect Author and Book (1:N)
tasks.description: Add foreign key authorId and relation field author to model Book.
instructions: In model Book, add authorId Int
tasks.solutionExplanation: Configures foreign key authorId referencing Author.id.
tasks.successMessage: Great job! 1:N relationship between Author and Book established.

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Optional 1:N Relation (Company & Employee)
tasks.description: Model 1-to-Many relation where companyId is optional (Int?) allowing unassigned employees.
instructions: In model Employee, add companyId Int?
tasks.solutionExplanation: Using Int? and Company? permits null foreign keys in SQL.

hints.text: Both companyId and company must have question marks (Int?, Company?).

tasks.successMessage: Well done! Optional foreign keys correctly configured.

concepts.title: One-to-One (1:1) Relations
concepts.shortDescription: The foreign key in a 1:1 relation MUST be unique to guarantee exclusivity.

theory.summary: A 1:1 relationship links one entity to at most one other entity (e.g. User and Profile). Syntactically, it is identical to 1:N, with ONE vital requirement: the foreign key MUST have @unique.

targetHero.explanation: @unique on userId transforms what would be a 1:N relation into a strict 1:1 relation.

explanation: Without @unique: Multiple Profile rows could have the same userId, making it 1:N.
With @unique: The database rejects duplicate userId entries, guaranteeing exactly 1:1.
theory.keyTakeaway: Always place @unique on the foreign key field in a 1:1 relationship.

mcqs.question: What happens if you omit @unique on the foreign key of a 1:1 relation?
options: Prisma schema validation throws an error because the relation is ambiguous
The database deletes the parent record
mcqs.explanation: Prisma compiler throws: "A one-to-one relation must have a unique constraint on the foreign key".

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Connect Account and AccountSettings (1:1)
tasks.description: Create a 1:1 relation between Account and AccountSettings, enforcing @unique on accountId.
tasks.solutionExplanation: accountId @unique guarantees only one AccountSettings row per Account.

tasks.title: Task 2 (Independent): Fix 1:1 Unique Constraint Bug
tasks.description: Fix a schema error where omitting @unique caused Prisma compiler failure.
instructions: Add @unique to driverId in model License
tasks.solutionExplanation: Adding @unique resolves the relation ambiguity and enables 1:1 navigation.
tasks.successMessage: Great fix! Driver to License is now a valid 1:1 relation.

concepts.title: Many-to-Many (M:N) Relations (Implicit vs Explicit)
concepts.shortDescription: Choose between Prisma-managed implicit join tables and explicit models with extra metadata.

theory.summary: In implicit M:N relations (Post[] and Tag[]), Prisma manages a hidden join table automatically. When the relationship needs its own data (e.g. assignedAt, role, grade), use an explicit join model with @@id([a, b]).

targetHero.explanation: PostTag stores extra metadata (assignedAt) between Post and Tag.

explanation: Implicit M:N: Easy and clean when no relation attributes are needed.
Explicit M:N: Essential for audit trails, permissions, timestamps, or quantities in shopping carts.
theory.keyTakeaway: If the relationship has attributes of its own, use an explicit join model.

mcqs.question: When MUST you use an explicit Many-to-Many relation instead of an implicit one?
options: When the relationship itself needs to store additional data (e.g. assignedDate, quantity)
Whenever there are more than 100 rows in the database
When models have more than 5 fields
mcqs.explanation: Implicit join tables cannot store extra columns. You must create an explicit join model to hold relation fields.

tasks.title: Task 1 (Guided): Define Implicit M:N Relation (Post & Category)
tasks.description: Define an implicit M:N relation between Post and Category by placing array relation fields on both models.
instructions: In model Post, add categories Category[]
In model Category, add posts Post[]
tasks.solutionExplanation: Prisma handles the underlying _CategoryToPost join table transparently.

hints.text: Add "categories Category[]" to Post and "posts Post[]" to Category.

Add relations to Student and ClassRoom
tasks.solutionExplanation: Explicit join model holding studentId, classRoomId, and custom grade attribute.

hints.text: Include student Student @relation and classRoom ClassRoom @relation.

tasks.successMessage: Masterful! Explicit M:N join model accurately crafted.
